title: OpenCTEM extension namespace, revision 2
description: The value of extensions["io.openctem"] on a report, metadata, asset, finding or rule: data only the OpenCTEM receiver profile defines (docs/profiles/openctem.md). A receiver that does not know the namespace ignores it. Revision 2 is the CTIS 2.0 revision; these keys are no longer read from properties.

capability.description: On metadata: the OpenCTEM capability the report answers, as id@major (scan.ports@1). A producer claim; the receiver uses the capability of the command it bound the report to.

import_scope.description: On an asset from an importer: whether the asset belongs to the import's target. The receiver decides scope; the importer never drops an outside asset.

candidate_exposure.description: On an asset: an exposure a tool suspects but did not verify. The receiver verifies before it alerts.

candidate_unverified.description: On an asset with candidate_exposure: true while nobody verified it.

bounty_report.description: On a finding from a bug-bounty or disclosure report: intake, ref, researcher (personal data), submitted_at, reported_severity, state, weakness, endpoint_path, parameter, url (https only, never fetched), reward and disclosure.

compliance_outcome.description: On a compliance finding of kind not_applicable: why the check was not evaluated. error: the check could not run (its message is the finding's message); skipped: the scanner skipped it. A receiver keeps an error as its own state, never as not applicable.

verification_hold.description: On a finding: the producer's screen of the matched response says the match may be the target's throttling or block answer, not the application. The receiver keeps the finding, holds it out of scores, SLA, notifications and tickets until it is checked, and never drops it. reasons: edge_block_page (a challenge, block or rate-limit page), throttled_response (429 or 503, or a Retry-After), soft_404 (resembles the origin's not-found answer), target_throttled (the target throttled or blocked the scan around the match), timing_based (the check decides on response time), oob_weak (a DNS-only, late or resolver-sourced out-of-band interaction). status, edge, edge_vendor and similarity are the screen's inputs; nothing of the response body is carried.

status.description: HTTP status of the matched response.

edge.description: How an edge protection answered in the origin's place.

edge_vendor.description: An open token naming the edge protection, shown as text only.

similarity.description: Similarity of the matched response to the origin's not-found answer (1: the same).

web_content.description: On a web_origin asset: the captures of a web content fetch. Each item: url, final_url (http or https), status_code, content_type, size, sha256, truncated, body (text, at most 512 KiB), body_truncated, fetched_at.

rule_source.description: On a rule: who authored it in OpenCTEM, a tenant (its own rule) or the platform.

ignore_file_paths.description: On metadata from a CI scan: the path patterns of the repository's scanner ignore file (plain relative patterns, never opened). OpenCTEM turns them into pending suppression requests on verified default-branch runs; they never suppress anything by themselves.
